instruction: `werkzeug.test.create_environ(*args, **kwargs)` is a thin wrapper that only builds an `EnvironBuilder` and returns its environ, and having two spellings for the same thing confuses users. Remove `create_environ` from `werkzeug.test` (delete the function; do not keep an alias or a deprecated shim) and rewrite every use in the repository, tests included, as `EnvironBuilder(<same arguments>).get_environ()`, passing exactly the arguments the call passed before (positional and keyword). Fix the imports of every module that used it: import `EnvironBuilder` from `werkzeug.test` instead, without duplicating an existing import. Test names stay as they are. Behavior must not change.
gold_tool: build_deep.py recipe: masked-text call finder (deep_edit) rewrites each create_environ(...) call to EnvironBuilder(...).get_environ(); AST removes the def; import lines rewritten; werkzeug's test suite in docker confirms
change: remove a helper function and inline its replacement at every call site (+ import fixes)
notes: All callers are tests; the green layer is werkzeug's full suite.

problem_statement: `werkzeug.test.create_environ(*args, **kwargs)` is a thin wrapper that only builds an `EnvironBuilder` and returns its environ, and having two spellings for the same thing confuses users. Remove `create_environ` from `werkzeug.test` (delete the function; do not keep an alias or a deprecated shim) and rewrite every use in the repository, tests included, as `EnvironBuilder(<same arguments>).get_environ()`, passing exactly the arguments the call passed before (positional and keyword). Fix the imports of every module that used it: import `EnvironBuilder` from `werkzeug.test` instead, without duplicating an existing import. Test names stay as they are. Behavior must not change.
